LESSON: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING - FICTIONAL AND NON-FICTIONAL

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional, part of Strand 9 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we relate events in a text with real life, people or places? 2. How can we predict what will happen in a text or story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. predict events by studying the title, cover or pictures in a text on lifestyle diseases,

2. picture events, characters or places in their minds,

3. read texts of up to 500 words related to the selected theme,

4. connect events in a text with an occurrence in their own life or real world events,

5. use the image on the front cover to predict events in the text,

6. infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as fixed phrases, idioms, proverbs and phrasal verbs,

7. retell the events depicted in a text in their own words. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. predict events by studying the title, cover or pictures in a text on lifestyle diseases,
2. picture events, characters or places in their minds,
3. read texts of up to 500 words related to the selected theme,
4. connect events in a text with an occurrence in their own life or real world events,
5. use the image on the front cover to predict events in the text,
6. infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as fixed phrases, idioms, proverbs and phrasal verbs,
7. retell the events depicted in a text in their own words. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: The learner’s ability to be self-driven and perform tasks on their own is enhanced as they

engage in self-driven tasks by inferring the meaning of unfamiliar words and phrases.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner comes up with unique and new ideas through creation of mind maps using

words in a text.

Values:
Responsibility: The learner proactively solves problems by connecting events in a text with an occurrence in their

own life or real world events.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Lifestyle diseases: The learner is able to make life changing decisions on health as they interact with information on

lifestyle diseases by reading texts on the themes.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of creating mental images from viewed, heard or read text to the concept of

drama techniques in Creative Arts.
